WEEK TWO
TOPIC: PACKAGING IN AGRICULTURAL
CONTENT
- Meaning of Packaging
- Purpose of Packaging
- Criteria for selecting packaging materials
- Types of packaging materials
MEANING OF PACKAGING
Packaging is the act of wrapping or enclosing agricultural products in a suitable material that will protect them when they are being transported from farms to markets and displayed in shops for people to buy.
PURPOSE OF PACKAGING
- To protect the product from being damaged when they are transported from the farm to the stores and markets.
- To protect farm products from damage as a result of bad weather, heat and rain.
- To protect farm products from contamination and damage by pests and disease organisms.
- Packaging makes agricultural products easier to handle, store and more attractive in shops.
- To prevent products from losing their value.
EVALUATION
- What is packaging?
- List five purposes of packaging.
CRITERIA FOR SELECTING PACKAGING MATERIALS
- The packaging material must be suitable for the type of agricultural products.
- Packaging material for animal products should be different from materials used for packaging plants.
- It must be capable of preventing farm products from breakage, leakage and damage to the farm.
- The packaging container must enclose the product in a convenient unit for handling and distributing.
- It must be strong enough to protect the agricultural products from hazards during transportation.
- It must be easily available and cheap.
- It must make it easy to carry the Agricultural products in terms of weight and form.
- It should be easy to dispose off after use.
TYPES OF PACKAGING MATERIAL FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
- Jute or Calico Sacks:  For packaging dried Agricultural products such as maize, rice, cowpea, millet, sorghum, dried cocoa, beans e.t.c.
- Plastic or Polythene bags: Used for packaging flour products such as: maize flour, cassava flour e.t.c
- BownKrafts: Used for packaging small quantity of dried grains e.g rice, beans, maize e.t.c. displayed for sale on shop shelves
- Cardboard Boxes and Trays: For packaging products such as eggs, pineapples, mangoes and bananas.
- Hard Plastic Containers: They are manufactured specially for carrying vegetables.
- Plastic Wrappers: Used for wrapping breed, for dressed chicken for sale in shops and markets.
- Wooden Crates: For packaging fresh fruits such as tomatoes, mangoes, avocado pear e.t.c
- Plastic Bottles: For packaging liquid such as vegetable oil, milk e.t.c.
- Glass Bottles and Jars: For packaging liquid such as honey, palm wine, Coconut Oil, Palm Oil e.t.c.
- Metal Drums and Cans: Metal drums are used to package large quantities of liquids vegetable Oil eg Palm Oil, Corn Oil. Metal Cans are used for packaging fish such as Sardines and Mackerels.
- Baskets: They are made locally fromraphia, palm frond e.t.c. They are very useful in packaging fruits and vegetables.
GENERAL EVALUATION
- What is Packaging?
- List three purpose of packaging.
- List three criteria for selecting packaging materials.
- List five packaging materials.
- List five items that a basket can be used to package.

WEEK THREE
TOPIC: BRANDING LESSON NOTE
CONTENT
- Definition of Branding
- Advantages of Branding
- Disadvantages of Branding
DEFINITION OF BRANDING
This is the activity of giving a particular name and lineage to goods and services, so that people will be attracted to them and want to buy them.
ADVANTAGES OF BRANDING
- It helps in easy identification of agricultural product.
- It helps the buyer to easily remember what they want to buy.
- It adds a measure of prestige to the product.
- It helps in maintenance of quality.
- The producer may enjoy some forms of monopoly when goods are branded.
- It prevents product adulteration.
- It helps to increase sales (turn over) of farm produce.
DISADVANTAGES OF BRANDING
- It increases the cost of production.
- Some products are difficult to brand e.g vegetables and fruits.
- It causes confusion among the consumers.
- Producers do find it difficult to maintain consistent quality.
GENERAL EVALUATION
- What is branding?
- List three advantages of branding.
- List three disadvantages of branding.

- List two purposes of advertisement.

TOPIC: PRICING OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
CONTENT
- Meaning of price
- Meaning of Market
- The concept of demand and supply
- Factors that determine Pricing of Agricultural Produce.
MEANING OF PRICE
The price of an agricultural product is the amount of money which a product is to be paid by people who desire to buy the products.
MEANING OF MARKET
A market is described as the specific place where producers and buyers meet for exchange of materials. The price of any agricultural product depends on the environment which is called.
EVALUATION
- What is Price?
- What is a Market?
THE CONCEPT OF SUPPLY AND DEMAND
Supply: The supply of a product is the total quantity of the product that producers offer for sale in the market.
Demand: The demand of a product is the total quantity of the product desired by all traders and customers for the product.
DETERMINATION OF PRICE BY SUPPLY AND DEMAND
If the supply of an agricultural product is low, which means there is a shortage of the product in the market, many people will want the product and some traders and customers will be prepared to pay extra money to buy the product. In this situation, the price of the product will be high.
When the supply of an agricultural product is high, it means there is a large quantity of the product in the market; some producers will be willing to sell for a low price, to attract buyers. The price of the product will therefore be low.
EVALUATION
- Define demand and supply.
- Explain how demand and supply affects prices.
FACTORS THAT DETERMINE PRICING OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE
- Cost of production: the production costs are put into consideration to fix the selling price of any agricultural produce.
- Quantity of Produce: if the farmer produces a large quantity of produce to make the market saturated the selling price will fall, vice versa.
- Quality of produce: the demand for high quality produce is high, therefore the selling price of such produce is also high.
- Demand and supply.
- Market Places: the farther the distance to the site of production, the higher the selling price. Also farm produce sells more in cities than villages where the demand is low.
- Seasons: The prices of crops are low at their seasons of production and high when their season is gone.
GENERAL EVALUATION
- What is demand?
- What is supply?
- What is a market?
- Explain how demand affects pricing.
- List 5 factors that determine Pricing.

WEEK  FIVE
TOPIC: ADVERTISING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE
CONTENT
- Meaning of Advertisement
- Purpose of Advertisement
- Method of Advertisement
THE MEANING OF ADVERTISEMENT
This is the act of making people to know about agricultural products that are being produced and marketed by individuals and organisations.
PURPOSE OF ADVERTISING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
- To attract people to buy the product.
- To create awareness about the farm produce available.
- To make customers develop interest in the farm produce.
- To increase the income of the agricultural product.
METHODS OF ADVERTISING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
Agricultural products are advertised through the following means:
- Local newspaper.
- Mass media such as radio and Television.
- The bill boards.
- Use of handbill, pamphlets and bulletins.
- Through the social media such as Facebook, instagram etc.
- Through mobile phones.
Information provided to advertise agricultural products are:
- The common trade name of the product.
- The high qualities of the product.
- Where the product can easily be obtained.
GENERAL EVALUATION

- Define Advertisement.

WEEK SIX
TOPIC: MARKETING IN AGRICULTURE LESSON NOTE
CONTENT
- Meaning of market and marketing
- Agricultural marketing activities
- Types of marketing for Agricultural Produce
MEANING OF MARKET AND MARKETING
A market is a place where farmers exchange agricultural produce such as yams for money.
Agricultural marketing involves all activities from gathering of agricultural produce from farms to getting them to the customers.
AGRICULTURAL MARKETING ACTIVITIES
This involves the activities such as assembling, grading, processing, packaging, storage, transportation and distribution.
- Assembling: this involves collection of products from various locations in order to make them available in large quantity for the buyers.
- Grading: Products are sort into grads depending on their shape, size, quality, purity, flavor etc. this is done to ensure high standards of agricultural products.
- Processing: Processing is the conversion of farm product into a better form to increase the utility and value. E.g orange can be processed to orange juice.
- Packaging: This involves the placing of farm products in crates, boxes or egg containers. This makes transportation easy to carry out.
- Storage: Farm produce are preserved and kept to make it available to consumers most of the time.
- Transportation: It is necessary to move agricultural produce from the farm to the market so that the customers can find them to buy.
- Distribution: Traders, wholesalers and retailers are involved in the distribution of farm produce to their customers.
EVALUATION
- What is marketing?
- List and explain five marketing activities.
TYPES OF MARKETS FOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE
- Perfect competition market: In this type of market, there are many buyers and sellers.
- Imperfect competition: The decision of one or more sellers or buyers affects the price of the commodity. The forms of imperfect market are:
- Monopoly:  When there is one seller and more buyers.
- Duopoly:  When there are two sellers.
- Oligopoly:  Where there is a small numbers of sellers.
- Monopsony:  When there is only one buyer.
- Duopsony:  When there are two buyers.
- Oligopsony: When thereare small number of buyer.
GENERAL EVALUATION

- What is marketing?

WEEK SEVEN
TOPIC: FARM RECORDS LESSON NOTE
CONTENT
- Meaning of Farm Records
- Purpose of Keeping Farm Records
- Types of Farm Records
MEANING OF FARM RECORD
Farm record is the documentation of various events which happens on a farm.
Purpose of Keeping Record
- It is useful for future planning
- It can be used as part of collateral for loan
- It helps the farmer to know whether he is making a profit or loss
- It helps the farmer to know the state of things on the farm
- It helps to detect fraudulent acts
- It help in farm management decision taking.
EVALUATION
- What is farm record?
- List two purpose of keeping farm records
TYPES OF FARM RECORDS
The types of farm records include; farm dairy, farm inventory, input records, production records, sales record, and consumption records e.t.c.
- The Farm Diary
This contains the record of day-to-day events on the farm. This includes the dates of planting, germination, flowering, the amount of farm input such as pesticides, fertilizer and so on, the date of birth of the younganimals etc.
- The Farm Inventory
This is the record of all the property and resources in the farm which are owned by the farmer, these includes the building, livestock, machines, equipment and so on.
- Input Records
This is the record of all inputs used for production in the farm during the year; these includes the cost of seeds, cost of feeds, cost of drugs, cost of tools, cost of equipment e.t.c.
- Production Records
This is the record of all items produced on the farm. Such items include the crops and livestock.
- Consumption Records
This is the record of all farm products consumed by the owner of the farm.
- Sales Records
This is the record of the sales on the farm; it enables the farmer to know whether he is making profit or loss.
GENERAL EVALUATION

- List three purpose of advertisement

WEEK EIGHT
TOPIC: BOOK KEEPING
CONTENT
- Meaning of Book Keeping
- Source Document
- Journals
BOOK KEEPING
This is the act of recording business transaction in a systematic manner so that the books will show at any time the exact state of their owners affairs.
SOURCE DOCUMENT
They are those documents that form the source of book keeping records. They are documents of initial transactions from which book keeping records are made or kept.
EVALUATION
- What is Book Keeping?
- What are source document?
TYPES OF SOURCE DOCUMENTS
- Sales Invoice: These are out going invoice.
- Purchase Invoice: These are incoming invoice issued by the creditors or suppliers.
- Receipt: This is evidence of cash payment.
- Voucher: This is the evidence of payment or receipt with a brief detail in respect of the transaction.
- Credit note: This is sent to inform the receiver that this account is credited as a result of an overcharge.
- Debit note: It shows that the receiver’s account is debited as a result of undercharge e.t.c.
JOURNALS
These are the books of original entry, that is, where transactionare first recorded before they are transferred to the ledger. They are also called the subsidiary books or books of prime entry. They can be listed as follows,
- Cash  book/Cash account
- Sales book / Sales day book/Sales Journal
- Purchases book/purchases day book/Purchase journal
- Return inward book / Sales return book / Sales return journal
- Purchases returns book/return outward book/Return outward journal
- General journal /Principal journal / Journal proper
GENERAL EVALUATION
